questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: It is illegal in Iowa for any driver to read, write, or send a text message while driving.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: In Iowa, it is illegal for any driver to read, write, or send a text message while driving. You must safely stop your vehicle off the road before using a phone or other device to send or read a text message.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down, move out of the way, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: You should still wear your seat belt.
You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You should wear your seat belt behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should still wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For the best protection in a crash, you should use both your seat belt and airbags together.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder at your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder at your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first. Then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no other vehicle is trying to enter the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine treat a cold.
The combination can multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can multiply the effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase how much both affect your body. For example, one drink with a cold medicine can impair you as much as several drinks without medicine.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, it is important to remember that trucks:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other drivers are doing instead of following the guard's directions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard in a school zone. Be ready to slow down when directed by a sign, guard, or police officer. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden under the seat.
Stops the seat belt warning light from turning on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is coming. Be alert for traffic from other directions.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are turning.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights tell other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Driving too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you move your vehicle. Check it when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other vehicles are nearby.
Is a good habit and is required by law.
Is only necessary during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, a driver should yield the right-of-way.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way. They have the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful near children. Always yield to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you drive better.
Make you feel better.
Impair your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Impair your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: If you are in a serious motor vehicle crash, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Call 911 if anyone is injured and help them. You must report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are to the right.

questions.question: Because county highways often have slow-moving traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay in the left lane and drive faster than the speed limit.
Be ready to adjust your speed to match traffic.
Pass slow-moving vehicles while in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to adjust your speed to match traffic.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to spot slow-moving vehicles early. This gives you time to change lanes or slow down safely. Always adjust your speed to match traffic within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, wait until you can see the entire car in your rearview mirror before moving back into the right lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: After passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see the entire vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road can become wet and slippery.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Do this along with adjusting your seat, fastening your seatbelt, and securing any items. Never adjust mirrors while the car is moving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most children are done exiting the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before turning.

questions.question: What should a driver watch?

options.text: Only straight ahead in front of the car.
Only the middle of the road.
Beside, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beside, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches beside, ahead, and behind the car. You need to know what is happening all around your vehicle.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive around the pedestrians on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking a non-prescription drug?

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive safely. Check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: Alcohol affects your ability to drive by causing:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol impairs your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.
